solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fuss about daughter having lover

parts.note: fuss and ado both mean a commotion or bother
re is a Latin-derived word for about or concerning
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A parent kicks up a fuss on learning that their daughter has a boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: to be adored is to have someone who loves you, so 'having lover' stands for the past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adored is loved dearly, so they are a person with an admirer devoted to them.

clue.text: A group of musicians on leave

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A band of musicians is on leave from touring.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon is to leave or desert someone or something.

clue.text: Finished with a sense of failure

parts.note: something finished is over
sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Someone is done with life, having a feeling of defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a failure to notice something, a lapse or omission.

clue.text: Lie, say, is found out without difficulty

indicators.note: found out in the sense of exposed and disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lie is exposed with no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link; 'found out' rearranges LIE SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily means with ease, done with no difficulty.

clue.text: Bulletin carelessly pasted to front of church

indicators.note: says the rearranged letters are attached ahead of the church abbreviation
something done carelessly is jumbled, so the letters of pasted are rearranged

explanation.surface: A notice has been stuck up sloppily on the front of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A despatch is an official report or news story sent from abroad, a kind of bulletin.

clue.text: His influence may make Rose change her name

definitions.text: His influence may make Rose change her name

indicators.note: change tells us the letters of Rose swap places

explanation.surface: Love leads a woman called Rose to take a new surname when she marries.
explanation.walkthrough: Whole clue: the god of love can lead Rose to marry and take a new surname, and 'change' rearranges ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, whose influence leads people to marry.

clue.text: Claims an old city quarter provide a diversion

parts.note: pleas are claims or arguments put forward
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
E for east, one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: Arguments that an old city district should offer some entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is enjoyment or amusement, so a pastime or diversion.

clue.text: Refuse to start treating skin problem

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of treating

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of red spots on the skin

explanation.surface: A patient declines to begin treatment for a skin condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Trash is rubbish or waste, the noun sense of refuse.

clue.text: Asinine utterances

parts.note: asinine usually means foolish, but literally means of a donkey, whose bray is the sound meant

explanation.surface: Foolish remarks made by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey's bray is conventionally written as a two-part call, and asinine means donkey-like.

clue.text: Opposed States open engagement

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly, so 'states' gives avers

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, taken here from engagement

explanation.surface: Several states declare war openly against an enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means being opposed to or disinclined towards it.

clue.text: A love letter disposed to show forbearance

indicators.note: disposed in the sense of arranged, so the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone accepts a love letter with patience and good grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' rearranges A, O and LETTER together.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate something is to put up with it patiently, which is exactly showing forbearance.

clue.text: Conceal that the cost of insurance has risen

parts.note: cover is the protection an insurance premium pays for
something that has risen is up

explanation.surface: A firm hides the fact that insurance premiums have gone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover up is to hide or conceal something, especially wrongdoing.

clue.text: I'd turn a sickly colour and refuse permission

indicators.note: turn tells us to read the letters of I'd the other way round

parts.note: sallow describes a yellowish unhealthy complexion

explanation.surface: Someone says they would go pale with illness and so decline a request.
explanation.definitionFit: To disallow is to reject or forbid, so it means refusing to give permission.

clue.text: A maths formula which leaves one breathless

indicators.note: a formula is a fixed arrangement, so the letters of A maths are reordered

explanation.surface: A mathematical equation so hard it leaves a student gasping.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a respiratory condition whose attacks cause wheezing and shortness of breath.

clue.text: Moorish gentleman to rise with a greeting

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters of to read upwards, backwards

parts.note: hello is a greeting

explanation.surface: A gentleman from Morocco stands up to say hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns TO into OT. Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello, the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy, is a Moor serving Venice.

clue.text: Futile report on person lacking energy?

explanation.surface: A pointless school report about a pupil who never makes an effort.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading imagines a report saying a lazy person has no go, 'go' meaning energy or vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no-go is impossible or not worth attempting; having no go means lacking any drive.

clue.text: Yeasty reds drunk in the recent past

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and confused, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Frothy red wines were being drunk only lately.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterdays, as a noun, refers to days gone by, the recent past.

clue.text: Navigation aid gives boats real improvement

indicators.note: an improvement reworks things, so the letters of boats real are reordered

explanation.surface: A navigation device makes boats truly better.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrolabe is an old instrument for measuring star altitudes, used in navigation.

clue.text: Short skirt pretty girl's about to make shorter

indicators.note: about says the pretty girl goes around the skirt

parts.note: dish is slang for an attractive person
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: A pretty girl wearing a mini is about to shorten it further.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish is to reduce or lessen, making something smaller or shorter.

clue.text: Skills shown by artiste, but presented badly

indicators.note: something presented badly is put out of order, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A performer shows off talents but in a clumsy way.
explanation.definitionFit: Attributes are qualities or abilities a person has, so they can mean skills.

clue.text: Feeler from a National Trust girl taken up

parts.note: NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read upwards, so the girl's name reverses

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is recruited by the National Trust as a scout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns ANNE into ENNA. The National Trust is the British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is an insect's sensory feeler on the head.

clue.text: Opposition leader, a jerk, is of concern to the listener

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Opposition

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: The leader of the opposition has a nervous twitch that worries his audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is the medical adjective for things relating to the ear, which a listener uses.

clue.text: Admit to swindle over grant

parts.note: a con is a swindle
to cede is to grant or hand over

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to cheating over a grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places CON above CEDE in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede is to admit that something is true, often reluctantly.

clue.text: Conclude Luxembourg is somewhat rich and elegant

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An observer decides that Luxembourg is a wealthy, stylish country.
explanation.definitionFit: De luxe describes something luxurious and of superior quality, rich and elegant.

clue.text: Light meal for a pet at home

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, and so is a tiff
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Food set out for a family pet while the owners are in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' is not an animal here but a sulk or quarrel. TIFFIN is a light midday meal, a term from British India.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin is a light lunch or snack, a word from the Raj still used in India.

clue.text: Rural deity heads a list of animal life

indicators.note: heads means the deity comes on top of the a in this down entry

parts.note: a faun is a Roman god of the countryside, half man and half goat

explanation.surface: A country god tops a list of wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Fauna is the animal life of a region, as flora is its plants.

clue.text: Once in a lifetime phenomenon?

parts.note: the idiom for something very rare refers to a second full moon in one calendar month

explanation.surface: Asking about an event that happens only once in a person's life.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom once in a blue moon describes something happening very rarely.

clue.text: Sign of victory on hand

explanation.surface: A gesture of triumph made with one hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A palm frond was a classical token of victory; the palm is also the inner hand.

clue.text: A lunatic, crazy about boats

indicators.note: crazy says the letters of a lunatic are wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: A madman is obsessed with boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical means relating to ships, sailors or navigation, so concerning boats.

clue.text: Compassionate chap put in the shade

indicators.note: put in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: hue and shade both mean a colour
chap and man are both informal words for a male person

explanation.surface: A kind man is left standing in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means showing kindness and mercy, close to compassionate.

clue.text: A song about a subject a person cannot stand

indicators.note: about says the song goes round the small word a

parts.note: an anthem is a song, such as a national or church song

explanation.surface: A tune about a topic that someone simply hates.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital 'A' at the start supplies the final A; 'about' puts the lower-case 'a' inside ANTHEM to make ANATHEM.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is something or someone intensely loathed, a thing a person cannot bear.

clue.text: Cut off head of enemy — being ruthless

parts.note: to sever is to cut off

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of enemy

explanation.surface: A warrior beheads an enemy without mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means harsh and unsparing, close in sense to ruthless.
